clue.text: State of Virginia overturned election result originally

indicators.note: turned upside down, so in a down entry the abbreviation is read from the bottom up
originally points to the opening letter of each of the two words that follow

parts.note: the first letters of election and result

explanation.surface: An American state's disputed election result is overturned on appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like a US state alongside Virginia, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To aver is to declare or assert something firmly, a formal synonym of the verb to state.

clue.text: Trendy art movement censoring sadomasochistic nightmares

parts.note: in means fashionable

indicators.note: censoring cuts something out, so these letters are removed from the art movement

parts.note: Cubism, the movement of Picasso and Braque
SM is the usual shorthand for sadomasochism

explanation.surface: A fashionable art movement has its sadomasochistic content censored.
explanation.definitionFit: Incubi are demons said to lie on sleepers, and the word once meant nightmares themselves.

clue.text: Hard work pursuing computer operating system's browser activity?

indicators.note: pursuing means following, so the hard work comes after the operating system

parts.note: Windows is Microsoft's operating system
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Someone toils away on a Windows computer, using its web browser.
explanation.walkthrough: The browser is not software but a person browsing shop windows; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: To window-shop is to look at goods in displays without buying, which is what a casual browser does.

clue.text: Warm up expending energy — control bowler's rest?

indicators.note: expending means using up, so the energy letter is spent and drops out

parts.note: to heat is to warm up
to peg prices is to control them

explanation.surface: A cricketer warms up and then must control the bowling.
explanation.walkthrough: The bowler is not a cricketer but a bowler hat, which rests on a peg.
explanation.definitionFit: A hat peg is a hook on which a hat such as a bowler is hung when not worn.

clue.text: Writer to run away with Some Like It Hot actor

parts.note: a pen is a writing implement
to elope is to run away to marry
the surname is tucked across the words like it hot, some of the film title's letters

explanation.surface: A writer runs off with an actor from the film Some Like It Hot.
explanation.walkthrough: PENELOPE KEITH is an English actress best known for the sitcoms The Good Life and To the Manor Born.
explanation.definitionFit: Penelope Keith is a celebrated British stage and television performer, so actor fits her.

clue.text: Essential to bring up son's pornography

indicators.note: in a down entry, bringing something up lifts it out of its place and moves it to the top, so the son goes first

parts.note: something essential is a must, with its son taken out to be moved

explanation.surface: A parent insists it is vital to raise a son with no access to porn.
explanation.definitionFit: Smut is a slang word for obscene or pornographic material.

clue.text: Orchestra misbehave — less authentic in audition

parts.note: to sin is to misbehave

indicators.note: an audition is a hearing, so the words are judged by how they sound

parts.note: phonier means more fake, so less authentic

explanation.surface: An orchestra player behaves badly and seems a fraud at their audition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinfonia is used in the names of many small orchestras, such as the City of London Sinfonia.

clue.text: You and I will get healthy

parts.note: we covers the speaker and the person addressed
'll is the contracted form of will

explanation.surface: A cheerful promise that the two of us will get better.
explanation.walkthrough: Together the pieces make the contraction we'll, written without its apostrophe.
explanation.definitionFit: Well means in good health, as in 'I am feeling well'.

clue.text: Worried after pulse initially dropping 90% — getting air

indicators.note: the worried part comes after the pulse
the initial letter, Roman 50, falls to Roman 5, a ninety per cent drop in value

parts.note: a lentil is a pulse, an edible seed
ate as in 'what's eating you?', meaning worried

explanation.surface: A patient's pulse plummets, causing worry, and they are given air.
explanation.walkthrough: L is the Roman numeral 50 and V is 5, so swapping one for the other drops the value by 90%.
explanation.definitionFit: To ventilate is to supply fresh air to a room or a patient's lungs.

clue.text: To an American it sounds easy — I am returning sweetcorn

indicators.note: returning means turning back, so all the letters are read from right to left
Americans say the letter Z as zee, so the two letters E Z are heard as the word easy

parts.note: said aloud, the two letters e and zee sound like easy
taken as written

explanation.surface: An American finds sweetcorn easy to grow.
explanation.walkthrough: This works only with the American zee; the British zed would not sound like easy.
explanation.definitionFit: Maize is the plant whose cobs are eaten as sweetcorn, called corn in America.

clue.text: Group drinks stout

definitions.meaning: first meaning: drinks bought for everyone in a party at once

explanation.walkthrough: Stout looks like the beer being ordered, but it is the adjective for a portly figure.
explanation.definitionFit: A round is a set of drinks bought for a group, and round also means plump or chubby.

clue.text: Fill up ten churns — that's ample

indicators.note: churning stirs things up vigorously, so the letters are mixed together

parts.note: the nine letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Filling ten milk churns gives plenty of milk.
explanation.definitionFit: Plentiful and ample both describe a supply that is more than enough.

clue.text: Friend going around with good gossip

indicators.note: the friend goes around the abbreviation, holding it inside

parts.note: china is cockney rhyming slang for mate (china plate)

explanation.surface: A friend comes round with some juicy gossip.
explanation.walkthrough: In cockney rhyming slang china plate means mate, shortened to china.
explanation.definitionFit: A chinwag is an informal chat, the sort of talk in which gossip is swapped.

clue.text: Died, removing arrow — periodically being covered in mud, for example

indicators.note: removing takes these letters out of the slang word for died

parts.note: croaked is slang for died

indicators.note: periodically means at regular intervals, so every other letter is taken

parts.note: every other letter of arrow, the second and fourth

explanation.surface: Someone killed by an arrow lies in the mud.
explanation.definitionFit: Caked means coated with a thick hardened layer, such as dried mud on boots.

clue.text: It's natural I see when eye, say, opens

indicators.note: the organ opens the word, coming first

parts.note: the eye is an example of an organ
IC sounds like 'I see' when the letters are said

explanation.surface: A natural reaction is to understand once your eyes are opened.
explanation.definitionFit: Organic produce is grown naturally, without artificial chemicals.

clue.text: Brokers try and gamble on small ones occasionally

parts.note: a go is an attempt
to bet is to gamble
wee is Scottish for small

indicators.note: occasionally means now and then, so alternate letters are taken

parts.note: every other letter of ones, the second and fourth

explanation.surface: Stockbrokers take a punt and bet on small companies now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: Go-betweens are intermediaries who negotiate for others, as brokers do.

clue.text: Farm acre in the middle of Dorset, at last

indicators.note: only the middle letters are kept, losing both ends

parts.note: acre without its first and last letters
taken as written

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the county name

parts.note: the final letter of Dorset

explanation.surface: An acre of farmland right in the centre of Dorset, an English county.
explanation.definitionFit: A croft is a small rented farm, especially in the Scottish Highlands.

clue.text: See 5
Offering protection where female goes to be browsing the internet

parts.note: in is a word saying where something is

indicators.note: the clue is read in reverse: the female letter goes into the answer's gap to make the phrase for browsing

parts.note: surfing is browsing the web

explanation.surface: An insurer offers cover wherever a woman goes online.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works backwards: the answer plus F gives IN SURFING, which is where one is when browsing the internet.
explanation.definitionFit: Insuring means providing cover against loss, a form of financial protection.

clue.text: Cost of iron ore, not gold

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

indicators.note: not means without, so the gold letters are removed

parts.note: taken as written, before the gold is removed
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: The price of iron ore, as opposed to gold ore.
explanation.definitionFit: A fee is a charge or payment for a service.

clue.text: Enthusiasts accepting ticket price for trumpets

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the price goes inside

parts.note: fans are enthusiasts
a fare is the price of a ticket

explanation.surface: Supporters take on the ticket price for a trumpet concert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trumpets' is a verb here, as in proclaiming.
explanation.definitionFit: To fanfare something is to herald it loudly, which is what trumpeting it means.

clue.text: Live with an old comic

parts.note: to be is to exist, to live
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone lives with an old comic book.
explanation.walkthrough: The Beano is a long-running British children's comic, home of Dennis the Menace.
explanation.definitionFit: The Beano is a comic magazine, and a beano is also slang for a party.

clue.text: Desperate Dan puts shovel …

indicators.note: desperate suggests wild disorder, so the letters are thrown about

parts.note: the seven letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Desperate Dan, the comic-strip cowboy, puts a shovel into the earth.
explanation.walkthrough: Desperate Dan is a strongman in the British comic The Dandy; the ellipsis runs on into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A dustpan is a flat shovel-like scoop into which dirt is swept.

clue.text: … in earth, moving about hundred tons — it only allows travel in one direction

definitions.text: it only allows travel in one direction

indicators.note: the rearranged earth goes about the hundred, enclosing it
moving shifts the letters around

parts.note: the five letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Desperate Dan shovels a hundred tons of earth around.
explanation.definitionFit: A ratchet is a toothed mechanism with a pawl that lets a wheel turn only one way.

clue.text: After missing Trigger's entrance once perhaps Del Boy recalled witty response

indicators.note: called back, so the letters are taken in reverse
the surname is taken after losing one letter

parts.note: Derek 'Del Boy' Trotter was a character in the old sitcom Only Fools and Horses

indicators.note: entrance is the way in, the opening letter

parts.note: the first letter of Trigger, Del Boy's dim friend in the sitcom

explanation.surface: Without Trigger there, Del Boy once came back with a witty line.
explanation.walkthrough: Del Boy and Trigger are characters in the British sitcom Only Fools and Horses; only one of the surname's two Ts goes.
explanation.definitionFit: A retort is a sharp or witty reply.

clue.text: As a result of this dissent you must make second billion

indicators.note: an instruction to change one letter of the dissent into another

parts.note: heresy is dissent from orthodoxy

explanation.surface: A dissenter is ordered to make a second billion.
explanation.definitionFit: Hereby is formal legal language for 'by means of this' document or act.

clue.text: Maybe Frosty Morning's ordinary following trade wind

indicators.note: the ordinary letter follows the trade

parts.note: work is a trade or occupation
fart is slang for breaking wind

explanation.surface: A cold morning brings an ordinary wind to follow trade winds.
explanation.walkthrough: Frosty Morning is a painting by J M W Turner; 'trade wind' is split between two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A work of art is a painting or sculpture, and Turner's Frosty Morning is one example.

clue.text: PC World's opening — consent to having electronic support

indicators.note: in a down entry a support goes below, so the electronic letter comes last
the opening is the first letter

parts.note: the first letter of World, from the shop name PC World
to OK something is to consent to it

explanation.surface: The electronics shop PC World opens with electronic support on offer.
explanation.walkthrough: PC World is a British electronics retailer; here PC means politically correct.
explanation.definitionFit: Woke is a term, often disparaging, for politically correct alertness to social injustice.

clue.text: Working with axes to produce mineral

parts.note: on means operating, as a machine switched on
y and x are the axes of a graph

explanation.surface: A miner works with axes to dig out minerals.
explanation.walkthrough: The axes are not tools but graph axes.
explanation.definitionFit: Onyx is a banded variety of chalcedony, a mineral used in ornaments.

clue.text: Naughty child having time out for wrongdoing

indicators.note: time out means the time letter is taken out of the child

parts.note: a little terror is a naughty child

explanation.surface: A naughty child is given time out for misbehaving.
explanation.definitionFit: An error is a mistake or a moral fault, a lapse in correct conduct.

clue.text: Fish streams

definitions.meaning: first meaning: flat cartilaginous fish such as skates

explanation.walkthrough: Streams suggests water to go with the fish, but here it means streams of light.
explanation.definitionFit: Rays are flat sea fish and also narrow beams of light or radiation.

clue.text: Strange jet ski barely starts

indicators.note: the stripped ski starts the answer, coming first
bare means stripped, so the word loses its outer letters

parts.note: ski with its outer letters stripped leaves the middle one
jet is a deep glossy black, as inky is

explanation.surface: An odd sight: a jet ski that hardly gets going.
explanation.definitionFit: Kinky means peculiar or eccentric, usually with a sexual flavour.

clue.text: Servant revealed Queen essentially embarrassed by Andrew hiding evidence of sweat

indicators.note: by means next to, so the pieces sit side by side

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina

indicators.note: the essence of the word is its central letter

parts.note: the central letter of embarrassed, sixth of eleven

indicators.note: hiding means concealing inside, so the sweat evidence goes within the name

parts.note: Andy is short for Andrew
BO is body odour

explanation.surface: A servant reveals the Queen was embarrassed by Andrew's sweaty secret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revealed' just links the definition to the wordplay; Prince Andrew's claim that he could not sweat fuels the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: An errand boy is a youth employed to run messages and errands, a junior servant.
